chunks: And Amir al-Mu'minin عليه السلام said:

None of you should pray behind one afflicted with mutilation, nor one with leprosy, nor one with mental disorder, nor one upon whom a legal punishment has been carried out, nor the child of zina, and the Bedouin should not lead the Muhajir in prayer.

key_terms.الْأَجْذَمِ: one afflicted with mutilation or loss of limb
key_terms.الْمَحْدُودِ: one upon whom a prescribed legal punishment has been carried out
key_terms.خَلْفَ: behind, in following an Imam in prayer

ai.seo_question: Who should not be followed as an Imam in congregational salat (prayer)?
ai.summary: This hadith states rulings regarding who should not be followed in congregational salat (prayer). It addresses qualifications and restrictions for the Imam of congregational prayer, reflecting legal and social considerations in the conduct of communal worship.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.1105 - The Commander of the Faithful Imam Ali ibn Abi Talib (as) said:

"None of you should pray behind a person with a mutilated limb (al-ajdham), a person with leprosy (al-abrāṣ), a person with a mental disorder (al-majnūn), a person who has been subjected to a legal punishment (al-maḥdūd), the child of adultery (walad al-zina), or a Bedouin (al-a‘rābī) leading a migrant (al-muhājir)."
